nodes.title: The Fong–Swan theorem
nodes.statement: Let Γ be a finite p-solvable group (in particular any finite solvable group), k an algebraically closed field of characteristic p, and τ as in R17.5/brauer-character. Every irreducible Brauer character φ of Γ is the restriction to p-regular elements of an irreducible ordinary character: there is a complex irreducible representation with character χ such that χ(g) = φ(g) for every p-regular g. Equivalently (module form): for any splitting p-modular system (F, R, k₀) for Γ, every simple k₀Γ-module is the reduction modulo π of an RΓ-lattice. Isaacs's proof gives a p-rational χ (values in a cyclotomic field of conductor prime to p); for p odd this p-rational lift is unique. The conclusion need not hold without p-solvability; the A₅ example below witnesses this, without asserting a converse characterisation of p-solvable groups.
hypotheses: Γ is finite and p-solvable: it has a normal series whose factors are p-groups or p′-groups; finite solvable groups qualify.
k is algebraically closed of characteristic p; Brauer characters are taken with respect to τ.
Module form: (F, R, k₀) is a p-modular system in which F and k₀ are splitting fields for Γ (Webb §9.4).
proofSteps: equivariant-fong-swan supplies a p-rational ordinary lift for every prime. Its stronger stabilizer and degree assertion has an explicit induction with modular Clifford, coprime-index comparison and determinant-order extension.

For odd-p uniqueness use Isaacs Theorem 1.2, §6 proof pp. 180–181. Induct on group order while also proving that constituents on every normal subgroup of a p-rational χ with χ* simple are p-rational and have simple Brauer restriction. Pass to the combined conjugation/Galois stabilizer and ordinary inertia correspondent; if proper, apply the group induction. Otherwise the inertia group is normal, and modular Clifford forces it to be all of Γ, since an invariant simple inducing to a simple has index one. For the remaining restriction induction use a proper normal subgroup of N and either its O^p or O^{p′} quotient, applying p-rational-p-group-extension or coprime-index-lift-correspondence. These simultaneous restriction hypotheses justify the final maximal-normal-subgroup argument. Two lifts restrict to the same p-rational lift of a constituent, by induction, and the p-group or coprime-index correspondence then makes the lifts equal.

Module form from the character form: realise χ over F (a splitting field), take a full RΓ-lattice L in the realisation (Webb Corollary 9.4.7: span of the Γ-translates of a basis); by brauer-character-recognition (c) the Brauer character of L/πL is χ* = φ, and by (b) L/πL ≅ S.
acceptance: The two-dimensional simple module of S₃ in characteristic 2 lifts to the reflection representation of S₃, although 2 divides |S₃|.
For Γ of order prime to p the theorem is the classical bijection between simple modules in characteristic zero and characteristic p (Webb Theorem 9.4.11, p. 155), and every lift is unique.

For a cyclic p-group the only irreducible Brauer character is trivial, and its lifts are all p-power-order characters; for p odd the p-rational one is the trivial character, illustrating Isaacs's uniqueness.
p-solvability cannot be dropped: A₅ ≅ SL₂(F₄) has a two-dimensional irreducible Brauer character at p = 2 (its natural representation), but no irreducible complex character of degree 2.

nodes.title: Integral lifts of representations of finite solvable groups
nodes.statement: Let p be prime, Γ a finite solvable group, k an algebraically closed field of characteristic p and r: Γ → GL_n(k) an irreducible representation. There exist a number field E, a height-one prime λ of O_E above p, the localisation R = (O_E)_λ (a discrete valuation ring), a ring homomorphism f: R → k with kernel λR, a group homomorphism ρ: Γ → GL_n(R) and P ∈ GL_n(k) such that r(g) = P·f(ρ(g))·P⁻¹ for every g ∈ Γ. One may take E to contain the e-th roots of unity, e the exponent of Γ. If r is injective so is ρ, and in general ker ρ = ker r. The reduction is isomorphic to r itself, not only after semisimplification; neither p ∤ |Γ| nor n = 2 is assumed.
hypotheses: p is prime; Γ is a finite solvable group; k is algebraically closed of characteristic p.
r: Γ → GL_n(k) is a homomorphism whose representation on kⁿ is irreducible (equivalently absolutely irreducible, as k is algebraically closed).
proofSteps: finite-field-simple-descent gives a finite splitting field k₀ and a simple k₀Γ-module S₀ whose extension to the arbitrary algebraically closed k is isomorphic to r. This descends the module up to conjugacy, never the displayed entries. split-simple-scalar-extension proves the needed quotient and radical comparison under the split hypothesis, so no additional radical base-change theorem over F_p is assumed. R01.1’s F̄_p-only descent is not used and Webb 9.2.7 is not modified in characteristic p.

Take E = Q(ζ_{e(q−1)}) and λ above p. The characteristic-zero cyclotomic splitting theorem (InductionRestriction Layer 6; Webb 9.2.7) makes E a splitting field for Γ. Reduction is an isomorphism on μ_{q−1}, so κ(λ) contains F_q. A field extension of a splitting field is splitting; hence (E,(O_E)_λ,κ(λ)) is a splitting p-modular system. Embed κ(λ) in k extending k₀. This uses finite-field embeddings and the Dedekind localisations already represented by the baseline.

fong-swan (module form) gives an RΓ-lattice L with L/λL ≅ S₀ ⊗_{k₀} κ(λ). L is finitely generated and torsion-free over the discrete valuation ring R, hence free of rank n (Webb Lemma 9.4.6, Corollary 9.4.7); a basis gives ρ: Γ → GL_n(R).

Choose f: R → κ(λ) → k extending the given inclusion k₀ ⊂ k (possible since k is algebraically closed and κ(λ) is a finite extension of k₀). Then f∘ρ ≅ S₀ ⊗ k ≅ r, which gives P. If ρ(g) = 1 then r(g) = P·P⁻¹ = 1, so ker ρ ⊂ ker r. Running the construction for the faithful representation of the solvable quotient Γ/ker r and composing with the quotient map gives ρ with ker ρ = ker r; in particular ρ is injective when r is.
acceptance: Γ = S₃, p = 2, r the two-dimensional simple module: the lift is the reflection representation over Z[ζ₃] localised at 2, whose reduction is r.
Γ = GL₂(F₃), p = 3, r the identity representation over F₃ ⊂ F̄₃: a lift is the section into GL₂(Z[√−2]) of R17.5/octahedral-mod-three-application, with λ = (1 + √−2).
For Γ of order prime to p and n = 1 the lift is the Teichmüller lift of a character (R01.1/teichmuller-lift-of-a-residual-character).
Changing the basis of L changes P; entrywise equality r(g) = f(ρ(g)) is not part of the statement.

Let k be an algebraic closure of F_p(t), and conjugate a finite-field simple representation by a matrix involving t. Its entries can generate an infinite field. The assertion still holds through conjugacy; the proof must not assert that those displayed entries generate a finite field.

nodes.title: Reduction at an odd prime detects the determinant of an involution
nodes.statement: Let R be a commutative ring without zero divisors, k a field in which 2 ≠ 0, f: R → k a ring homomorphism and A ∈ GL₂(R) with A² = 1. If det f(A) = −1 then det A = −1. The same holds if only B = P·f(A)·P⁻¹ with det B = −1 is known, for some P ∈ GL₂(k). Consequently, for a homomorphism ρ: G → GL₂(R), an element c ∈ G with c² = 1 and a residual representation r̄ = P·(f∘ρ)·P⁻¹ with det r̄(c) = −1, one has det ρ(c) = −1. The hypothesis 2 ≠ 0 in k is necessary: in characteristic 2 the identity matrix has residual determinant 1 = −1 but integral determinant 1.
hypotheses: R is a commutative ring with no zero divisors; k is a field with 2 ≠ 0; f: R → k is a ring homomorphism.
A ∈ GL₂(R) satisfies A² = 1; P ∈ GL₂(k).
proofSteps: det(A)² = det(A²) = 1, so det A = ±1 in the domain R.
If det A = 1 then det f(A) = f(1) = 1, and 1 = −1 in k would force 2 = 0; hence det A = −1.
Conjugation by P does not change the determinant, which gives the residual-conjugacy form and the statement for ρ(c).
acceptance: Over Z, diag(1, −1) reduced modulo 3 is odd, and the lemma recovers that its determinant is −1.
The scalar matrix −I has determinant +1 in rank two, so a scalar involution is never odd.
Modulo 2 the identity matrix has residual determinant −1 = 1 while its determinant over Z is 1: the lemma fails without 2 ≠ 0.

nodes.title: Characteristic-zero lifts of residual representations with solvable image
nodes.statement: Let F be a number field, p a prime, k = F̄_p (or any algebraically closed field of characteristic p, with the discrete topology) and r̄: G_F → GL_n(k) a continuous absolutely irreducible representation whose image is solvable. There exist a number field E, a prime λ of E above p, R = (O_E)_λ, f: R → k with kernel λR, a homomorphism ρ: G_F → GL_n(R) with open kernel (so continuous for the discrete and for the λ-adic topology on GL_n(R)) and P ∈ GL_n(k) with r̄(g) = P·f(ρ(g))·P⁻¹ for all g ∈ G_F, such that: ker ρ = ker r̄ (so ρ has finite image isomorphic to that of r̄, cuts out the same field, and is unramified at every place where r̄ is); for every embedding E → C, ρ is irreducible over C; its image, and so its projective image, is solvable. If n = 2, p > 2 and r̄ is totally odd (det r̄(c_v) = −1 for every complex conjugation c_v at a real place v), then ρ is totally odd. This strengthens R17.5/odd-residual-lift: the reduction is r̄ itself, not only its semisimplification; F need not be totally real for the lifting part; and no projective lifting, Tate vanishing or Teichmüller twist is used. For p = 2 the oddness clause fails; the characteristic-two case is planned in layer R17.6 of this roadmap.
hypotheses: F is a number field; p is prime; k is algebraically closed of characteristic p, with the discrete topology.
r̄: G_F → GL_n(k) is continuous, absolutely irreducible, and r̄(G_F) is a solvable group.
Oddness clause: n = 2, p > 2, and det r̄(c_v) = −1 for the complex conjugations c_v at all real places v.
proofSteps: Continuity with discrete coefficients means ker r̄ is open and Γ = r̄(G_F) is finite (R01.1/finite-coefficients-and-finite-quotients).

Apply solvable-integral-lift to the inclusion Γ ⊂ GL_n(k), irreducible because r̄ is: this gives E, λ, R, f, an injective ρ_Γ: Γ → GL_n(R) and P. Put ρ = ρ_Γ ∘ r̄; then ker ρ = ker r̄ is open, so ρ is continuous, and r̄ = P·(f∘ρ)·P⁻¹.

Irreducibility over C: if ρ ⊗ C had a proper invariant subspace W, its character would be χ_W + χ_{W′} with both summands characters of nonzero representations; realising them over a finite extension of E and reducing lattices, brauer-character-recognition (c) would give r̄ at least two composition factors, contradicting (b) and the simplicity of r̄.
Oddness: for each real v, c_v² = 1; involution-oddness-under-reduction with the residual comparison P gives det ρ(c_v) = −1.
acceptance: For p = 3 and r̄: G_Q → GL₂(F₃) surjective and odd, one admissible lift is s∘r̄ with the section s of R17.5/octahedral-mod-three-application; the theorem produces some lift with the same kernel, not necessarily that one.
For p = 2 and r̄ with dihedral image the lifting part holds but the oddness clause does not: every characteristic-two residual representation has det r̄(c) = 1 = −1.
A residual representation with nonsolvable image, for example r̄ onto GL₂(F₅) ⊃ SL₂(F₅), is outside the statement; its finite lifts need not exist with the same kernel.

nodes.title: Residual representations with solvable image are automorphic of weight one
nodes.statement: Let F be a number field, p an odd prime and r̄: G_F → GL₂(F̄_p) continuous and absolutely irreducible with solvable image, and let ρ, λ, f, P be the lift of R17.5/odd-solvable-residual-lift. There is a unique cuspidal automorphic representation π of GL₂(A_F) with π_v ≅ π((ρ∨)_v) at every place v; it is unramified at every finite place where r̄ is unramified, its central character is det ρ read by arithmetic reciprocity, and the reduction of ρ along the lattice R² is r̄ (after conjugation by P). If F is totally real and r̄ is totally odd, then π is holomorphic of parallel weight one in Rogawski–Tunnell's sense: π_v is the weight-one limit π(1, sgn) at every real place. This is the residual modularity input of the solvable case of Boxer–Calegari–Gee–Pilloni, Proposition 10.1.3; it is R17.5/residual-lt-application with its lifting step proved. No statement about the level, ordinarity or a weight-two form is made here.
hypotheses: F is a number field; p is an odd prime.
r̄: G_F → GL₂(F̄_p) is continuous, absolutely irreducible, with solvable image; ρ, E, λ, R, f, P are as produced by odd-solvable-residual-lift.
Weight-one clause: F totally real and det r̄(c_v) = −1 at every real place v; 'holomorphic of parallel weight one' is Rogawski–Tunnell's definition (R17.5/tr-weight-one).
proofSteps: ρ is irreducible with finite solvable image (odd-solvable-residual-lift), and so is ρ∨. Apply R17.5/solvable-artin to ρ∨: it gives a cuspidal π matching ρ∨ in the geometric convention: in the dihedral case at every place (R17.5/dihedral-artin), in the tetrahedral and octahedral cases at every place by tetrahedral-artin-all-places and octahedral-artin-all-places. Uniqueness is strong multiplicity one (R16.4/strong-multiplicity-one).

Since ker ρ = ker r̄, ρ_v is unramified wherever r̄ is, so π_v is an unramified principal series there (R16.3/principal-series-parameter). Duality preserves the ramification kernel; geometric Frobenius on ρ∨ has the same eigenvalues as arithmetic Frobenius on ρ.

Weight one: at a real v, ρ(c_v) is an involution with det ρ(c_v) = −1 (oddness clause), hence non-scalar, ρ_v = 1⊕sgn and π_v ≅ π(1, sgn), which is Rogawski–Tunnell's π₁ (R17.5/tr-weight-one). Duality leaves the real involution unchanged. Since Art_arith = Art_geom⁻¹, the central character det(ρ∨)∘Art_geom is detρ∘Art_arith.
acceptance: In BCGP's situation (p = 3 or 5, F a totally real quadratic extension of the base field, r̄ = ϱ with determinant the inverse cyclotomic character, solvable image), the output is a parallel weight one cuspidal π with r̄ as residual representation; their subsequent passage to an ordinary weight-two form, which they take from Barnet-Lamb–Gee–Geraghty, is a separate input not supplied here.
If r̄ is even at some real place, the construction still gives π but its component there is π(1, 1) or π(sgn, sgn), not of weight one.
For p = 2 the theorem is not stated: the oddness clause fails, and the characteristic-two case is planned in layer R17.6 of this roadmap.

nodes.title: Odd residual representations of G_Q with solvable image come from weight-one newforms
nodes.statement: Let p be an odd prime and r̄: G_Q → GL₂(F̄_p) continuous, irreducible and odd (det r̄(c) = −1), with solvable image. Let ρ, λ, f, P be the lift of R17.5/odd-solvable-residual-lift (n = 2, F = Q). Then there is a normalised cuspidal newform g of weight one, level N = the Artin conductor of ρ and nebentypus det ρ (an odd Dirichlet character under reciprocity), with Galois representation ρ_g ≅ ρ; consequently the reduction of ρ_g along the lattice R² is isomorphic to r̄, and for every prime ℓ ∤ N, f(a_ℓ(g)) = tr r̄(Frob_ℓ) and f(det ρ(Frob_ℓ)) = det r̄(Frob_ℓ) (arithmetic Frobenius). The prime divisors of N are exactly the primes at which r̄ is ramified, p included when r̄ is ramified at p. This is Dieulefait–Pacetti's Theorem 1.3 (Langlands–Tunnell in odd characteristic), with the lifting step written out; N can exceed Serre's conductor of r̄, and no weight-two form is constructed here.
hypotheses: p is an odd prime; r̄: G_Q → GL₂(F̄_p) is continuous and irreducible (hence absolutely irreducible, F̄_p being algebraically closed), odd, with solvable image.
Frobenius elements are arithmetic, as in Deligne–Serre; det ρ is read as a Dirichlet character by class field theory.
proofSteps: odd-solvable-residual-lift gives ρ: G_Q → GL₂(R) ⊂ GL₂(C), irreducible, odd, with finite solvable image and ker ρ = ker r̄.

Apply R17.5/solvable-artin and the all-place refinements to ρ∨, obtaining π_v ≅ π((ρ∨)_v) in the geometric convention. At infinity π is the weight-one limit. At an unramified prime ℓ its standard factor is det(1−ρ(Frob_ℓ,arith)ℓ⁻ˢ)⁻¹, because geometric Frobenius is the inverse of arithmetic Frobenius and duality inverts the eigenvalues.

R17.5/q-weight-one (Weil–Langlands, Deligne–Serre Théorème 4.10) and R16.6/weight-one-classical-comparison give the normalised weight-one newform g of level N(ρ) and nebentypus det ρ with ρ_g ≅ ρ (Deligne–Serre Théorème 4.1 for the attached representation). In the arithmetic formulation of the classical dictionary, use the preceding factor identity, so the attached Galois representation is ρ, not ρ∨. Deligne–Serre Théorème 4.6 (p. 514) identifies the primitive level with the Artin conductor.

Reduction: ρ_g ≅ ρ and r̄ = P·(f∘ρ)·P⁻¹ give the trace and determinant congruences; as r̄ is absolutely irreducible, every stable lattice of ρ_g has reduction isomorphic to r̄ (R01.1/brauer-nesbitt). Ramification: ker ρ = ker r̄, and the Artin conductor exponent at ℓ is positive exactly when ρ is ramified at ℓ.
acceptance: For p = 3 and r̄ surjective onto GL₂(F₃), the theorem specialises to R17.5/octahedral-mod-three-application with some lift, not necessarily the section s used there.
For a dihedral r̄ induced from a character of an imaginary quadratic field, g is a theta series of that field.
An even r̄ (det r̄(c) = 1) is excluded: its lifts are even and do not come from holomorphic weight-one forms.

sourceIssues.locator: Proposition 10.1.3, proof, second paragraph (solvable case), printed p. 474 of the published IHÉS version
sourceIssues.printed: In the solvable case the proof obtains a totally odd lift to characteristic zero with finite solvable image of the representation ϱ of G_E (E a totally real quadratic extension of the base field), using only the list of finite subgroups of GL₂ over finite fields and Tate's projective lifting theorem (their reference Ser77, Theorem 4), and then invokes Langlands and Tunnell.
sourceIssues.correction: Tate's theorem lifts a projective representation into PGL₂(C) to GL₂(C) but says nothing about reduction modulo a prime above p; the argument needs a lift whose reduction is ϱ itself. The Fong–Swan theorem for the finite solvable image of ϱ provides such a lift over the localisation of a number field at a prime above p, with the same kernel as ϱ, and total oddness follows because p > 2 (R17.5/solvable-integral-lift, R17.5/odd-solvable-residual-lift).
sourceIssues.reason: Reduction of the Tate lift is defined only after embedding the finite projective image into PGL₂ of a p-adic ring compatibly with reduction, which the proof does not construct; for p dividing the order of the image (p = 3 with image A₄ or S₄, the case of the proposition with p = 3) no prime-to-p averaging argument is available. The conclusion of the proposition is correct.

review.reason: Collated the published Proposition 10.1.3, pp. 473–474. Its solvable argument combines subgroup classification with Tate and asserts a lift of the residual representation itself.
